text:
Mark Scheifele is now the Jets' all-time points leader, and he took the record in a fitting way: four points and a shootout goal in a 5-4 win at Chicago after Winnipeg had trailed by four, as Ken Wiebe of the Winnipeg Free Press wrote. He was named the NHL's first star of the week.

The month has been his best stretch of the season, 18 points in his last 10 games at nearly 22 minutes a night. The goals have lagged the chances, though: 7 on 9.0 expected. He keeps getting the looks, and goals tend to follow chances, so there's room for the scoring line to catch up with the playmaking.

That playmaking is the core of him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 11.8 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 99th percentile among forwards. The other side of the ledger is real too: Evolving-Hockey put opponents at 0.20 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice, bottom 3% of forwards. He's a high-wire center on a team that keeps coming back, and right now the comebacks are winning out.
headline: Scheifele stands alone in Jets history
